text: In eighteen fifty-four, a man rode a platform high above a crowd, and had the only rope cut. He was Elisha Otis. On top of his platform sat a curved steel spring, like the ones on a wagon, with the rope tied to its middle. The rope's pull kept the spring bent into a bow. And the rails beside it had teeth. When the rope was cut, the spring snapped flat. Its ends jammed into the teeth, and the platform stopped. All safe, gentlemen. That one idea made skyscrapers possible. And today's elevators still catch themselves the same way. Full video on my channel.
